description.narrative: The development objective of Tax Administration Modernization Project for Moldova is to improve revenue collection, tax compliance and taxpayer services. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Tax Policy Reform, will finance a comprehensive review of the legal framework including: (i) revisions to align Moldovan legislation on Value Added Tax (VAT) and Excise Duties in line with the European Union (EU)-Moldova Association Agreement; (ii) options to strengthen legislation and administrative practices to counter international profit shifting and base erosion risks for the Moldovan tax base and relevant capacity building in State Tax Service (STS) and Ministry of Finance (MoF); (iii) strengthening national tax legislation by ensuring consistency of primary and secondary lax legislation, access to tax rulings and improvements in administration of local taxes and fees. 2) The second component, Institutional Development, will support changes to STss organizational structure and strengthen back office functions. 3) The third component, Operational Development, will finance functions that deal directly with taxpayers. 4) The fourth component, Information Technology (IT) Infrastructure and System Modernization, will acquire and implement an Integrated Tax Management System that will unify IT support for all business functions including: user role management and security, transaction audit trails and logging, taxpayer registration, returns processing, accounting, payment processing, collections and enforcement, objections and appeals, audit, risk assessment, management reporting, case work flow, data warehouse and business intelligence tools, a document management system and a portal interface. 5) The fifth component, Project Management and Change Management,will finance: national and international consultants to support procurement, financial management and technical implementation; international advisors for IT project management, training and change management; and operating costs associated with the implementation of the Project
To support business survival and sustain employment in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, through temporary tax relief, and improve taxpayer services in the Republic of Moldova

title.narrative: Number of hits to the STS web-site

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved with results exceeded the target value</strong> The final target has been overachieved by 46%, as total number of hits to the STS website in 2023 reached 10.4 million compared to 7.15 planned. The data on the number of hits are related only to the STS’s new single website operational since April 1, 2021. The number of hits to the STS website has increased almost 3 times during the project lifetime.</p>

title.narrative: The Training Distance Learning System for the most important workflows developed

baseline.value: The list of training programs is not identified

target.value: All identified distance learning courses to support the most important workflows are developed and updated

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Achieved. </strong>The STS developed 12 core distance learning programs and put them on the MOODEL platform in 2020. Three out of twelve identified training programs were developed by STS with support from development partners, including the US Treasury (on Taxpayer Service Manual) and SIDA (under Institutional Cooperation Project (2018-2021).</p>
<p>The STS is strengthening the sustainability of results achieved under TAMP by developing new courses and continuous staff training. As of project closure, the total number of online training materials (including video guides; course materials; video recordings of the training sessions etc) increased to 347.</p>

actual.value: All (12) identified distance learning courses to support the most important workflows were developed

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved with results exceeding the target value.</strong> The final target has been overachieved as tax arrears decreased to 3.86 percent in 2023 compared to planned 6.48%. In 2023, the tax arrears reached – MDL 2,467.18 million of total revenues – MDL 63,992.88 million. Per the Results Framework in the original project paper, the indicator is measured as the share of tax arrears at the end of the year of tax revenues collected during the year. </p>

title.narrative: Ensured that supplies of goods by insolvent subjects are taxed with VAT on the reverse charge principle (PBC/DLI 2)

baseline.value: Due to the legal gap in provisions which stipulates the process of debt cancellation, at the time transfer of collected VAT insolvent subject does not have liquidity and this creates budget losses

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved. </strong>The Amendments to the Tax Code aimed at ensuring that supplies of goods by insolvent subjects are taxed with VAT on reverse charge principle were approved by the Parliament (Law #171 dated December 19, 2019) and came into effect on January 1, 2020.  </p>

actual.value: The adopted changes to the Tax Code came into effect

target.value: Satisfaction increase – 10% (compared to baseline) Final survey conducted with data disaggregated by gender. Results and suggests actions of the STS to address weaknesses are published on the STS website

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Not achieved. </strong>The STS conducted the final survey of legal entities and individuals in April – May 2023. The data of individual’s survey was disaggregated by gender. The final target against the baseline of 2018 have not been achieved. As per the 2023 final taxpayer survey, the satisfaction of legal entities decreased by 0.56 percent and that of individuals increased only by 2.82 percent. The reports with the results of the surveys and the 2023-2024 Action Plan prepared to address the weaknesses revealed during the final surveys are published on the STS’s website.  </p>

actual.value: Legal entities – 75.9%; Individuals – 71.1%. Satisfaction of legal entities decrease by 0.56%, and that of individuals increased by2.85%. Final survey results, conducted with data disaggregated by gender, and STss action plan to address the weaknesses revealed are published on the STS website.

title.narrative: PBC: Introduced an Electronic Taxpayer Survey Tool

baseline.value: No tool for taxpayers regular feedback is in place.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved. </strong>The STS developed the electronic taxpayer survey tool, trained 175 tax officials to work with the tool, piloted it during June 21-July 23, 2021, and put into operation on September 15, 2021. To date, the STS conducted 11 surveys through this tool, and introduced some improvements to the STS’s internal processes. In addition, 80 laptops for the purpose of e-taxpayer survey tool were procured under TAMP’s IPF part.</p>

actual.value: The e-taxpayer survey tool is in operational use

title.narrative: Increased nominal value of the specific and minimal excise for all tobacco products under tariff position 240220 (PBC/DLI 1)

baseline.value: Specific rates and minimum rates by types of tobacco products as set up in the Tax Code of Moldova in 2017

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved.</strong> The Amendments to the Tax Code aimed at increasing the specific rates and minimal excise rates for all tobacco products under tariff position 240220 were approved by the Parliament (Law #257 dated December 16, 2020) and came into effect from January 1, 2021.  </p>

title.narrative: PBC: Improved the usability of the STS website

baseline.value: There are two websites available (one for information only and another one for the submission of tax declarations by taxpayers); there are some gaps in the functionality of both websites.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>. The STS’s new single website with improved features (https://sfs.md/ro), including a friendly design for people with special needs is operational from April 1, 2021. Since 2022, the new single website has fully replaced two previous sites.</p>

actual.value: New STS website is used by taxpayers

title.narrative: PBC: Strengthened the capacity of the STS staff to deliver taxpayer services

baseline.value: There is no a Manual on Taxpayer Services, the staff had no specific trainings.

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Achieved.</strong> The STS developed the Manual on Taxpayer Services ( approved by the STS Order # 40 dated January 27, 2020). All eligible STS staff from all offices (709 persons) completed the Manual-based training in October 2020.</p>
<p>Further training sessions of STS staff on manual aspects are continued under the distance learning training system. </p>

actual.value: The Manual is implemented and all eligible staff of STS located in all offices were trained

title.narrative: Established legal frameworks and transparent mechanisms for implementing the temporary tax relief to businesses to mitigate for the negative fiscal impact of the COVID-19 pandemic (PBC 7)

baseline.value: Legal frameworks for mechanisms to sustain tax revenue collection through support to business continuity that ensured transparency are not available

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved.</strong> The legal framework for implementation of subsidy programs was established. It included two regulations: i) Regulation on implementation of subsidies for the payments of allowances/salaries, which set forth, inter alia, measures of eligibility verification and grievance mechanisms (MoF Order #58 dated April 29, 2020), and ii) Regulation on implementation of subsidies based on expanded VAT refund mechanism, which set forth, inter alia, measures of eligibility verification and grievance mechanism (MoF Order #76, dated June 20, 2020).  The MoF published on its website i) the completion report on the implementation of the payroll subsidy program in both Romanian (https://mf.gov.md/ro/content/rapoarte-1/) and English (https://mf.gov.md/en/content/reports-1) in December 2021, and ii) Interim report on VAT refund program implementation and Report on VAT refund program covering payments made for applications received from start of program until December 2020 in both Romanian (https://mf.gov.md/ro/content/rapoarte-2) and English (https://mf.gov.md/en/content/reports-2) in July 2022.</p>

actual.value: Legal frameworks have been established. Report on payroll and VAT subsidies program were made public

title.narrative: Maintained employment and business survival in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, by temporarily providing tax relief (PBC 6)

baseline.value: No government programs to support business continuity and sustain employment in the context of COVID-19 pandemic

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Achieved with results exceeding the target value.</strong> Per the Ministry of Finance’s published reports: i) 96% of beneficiaries of the Payroll Subsidy Program (or 399 firms) continued to operate and maintained employment at 99.8% as of December 2020 compared to April 2020 (https://mf.gov.md/en/content/reports-1), and ii) 94.6% of beneficiaries (657 firms) of VAT Refund Program continued to operate and maintained employment level of 85.8% in December 2020 compared to April 2020 (https://mf.gov.md/en/content/reports-2).</p>
<p>The results achieved show a  stable positive effect. According to the STS, as of the end of 2022, 95% of beneficiaries payroll subsidy program and 97% of VAT refund subsidy program continued their operation. </p>

title.narrative: Set foundation for future STS digital modernization strategy

baseline.value: No evidence based analysis to inform future IT modernization strategy

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Partially achieved. </strong>This indicator, introduced during the 2022 Restructuring, had two milestones – i) Completion of IT Tax Capability Gap Assessment for the tax administration, and ii) preparation of technical specifications for a new ITMS. The first milestone was partly achieved. The consulting company contracted by the STS to perform the assignment in February 2023 completed the STS IT Capability Gap Assessment in July 2023 and prepared the draft STS IT Capability Gap Assessment report. The STS was not fully satisfied with the report even after its several revisions and in view of the upcoming project closure terminated the contract on November 28, 2023. However, the draft report provides a good base to inform future STS’s decisions related to ITodernization. </p>
<p>The final target was not achieved. The development of technical specifications should be based on the outputs of the STS IT Capability Gap Assessment.</p>

actual.value: IT Capability Gap Assessment is completed with the inception report accepted by the STS and draft of the final Assessment report prepared and shared with the STS.
